planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, cool, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, sheltered from strong wind that can topple the tall flower spires; Mountain Wave is most reliably perennial in climates with moderate summer temperatures.

directions: Plant in average to moist, organically enriched, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, in a site sheltered from strong wind. 'Mountain Wave' (Atropurpurea Group) produces finely divided, bronze-tinged foliage topped in late summer into early fall by tall, dark-stemmed, fluffy spires of fragrant creamy-white flowers with a subtle purple tinge that sway gracefully above the clump. Like other Atropurpurea Group selections, it combines reliably with hostas, ferns, and other shade perennials, attracts late-season pollinators, and is generally left alone by deer and rabbits. Keep soil consistently moist, especially in warmer zones, as drought stress quickly scorches the foliage and flower spires.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; like other Actaea simplex selections, 'Silver Axe' resents hot, dry conditions and benefits from a cool root zone maintained with organic mulch.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. 'Silver Axe' (also known under the synonym 'Scimitar') is grown for its deeply cut, dark green foliage with a distinctive silvery-grey flush, topped in late summer to fall by slender, branching racemes of small white flowers typical of the species. As with other Actaea simplex selections, mulch to keep the root zone cool and moist, and site out of hot afternoon sun, which scorches the leaves. Combines well with hostas, ferns, and other fine-textured shade perennials; all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested.
